63231.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
63231.question_text: When Paul came to Rome, the first set of people to Whom he preached were the
63231.explanation:
When Paul arrived in Rome, he first preached to the Jews living there. This was in line with his usual practice of preaching to the Jews first before turning to the Gentiles.

Biblical Reference (Acts 28:17, RSV):

"After three days he called together the local leaders of the Jews; and when they had gathered, he said to them, ‘Brethren, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.’”

Paul explained his situation to them and later preached about Jesus Christ, but some of the Jews rejected his message. As a result, Paul then turned to the Gentiles (Acts 28:28).

63247.explanation:
The question "Therefore in the resurrection, whose wife shall she be of the seven? For they all had her." was asked by the Sadducees. This is found in:

Matthew 22:23–28 (RSV)
"The same day Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no resurrection; and they asked him a question..."

The Sadducees did not believe in the resurrection of the dead, so they posed this hypothetical question to challenge Jesus and ridicule the idea of resurrection.

63258.question_text: It was wrong for King Solomon to have married foreign women because
63258.explanation: The main reason it was considered wrong for King Solomon to have married foreign women was the concern that they would entice him to worship idols. In 1 Kings 11:1-4, it is stated that Solomon's many foreign wives turned his heart away from the Lord, leading him into idolatry. The principle emphasized here is the potential spiritual danger that comes from being unequally yoked with those who do not share one's commitment to God.

63267.question_text: How many months were the Israelites on forced labour in Lebanon allowed to spend at home for every month at the labour camp?
63267.explanation: According to the account in 1 Kings 5:13-14, during the construction of Solomon's temple, the forced labourers from the Israelites in Lebanon were allowed to spend one month at home for every two months of forced labour. This arrangement is mentioned in the context of Solomon's dealings with Hiram, the king of Tyre, for the supply of cedar and cypress timber for the construction of the temple.

63268.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
63268.question_text: Which of the following kings said, 'Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt?
63268.explanation:
The statement “Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt” was made by King Jeroboam after he made two golden calves and set them up in Bethel and Dan. He did this to stop the Israelites from going to Jerusalem (in the southern kingdom of Judah) to worship, thereby consolidating his rule over the northern kingdom of Israel.

1 Kings 12: 28 (RSV):

“So the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold. And he said to the people, ‘You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’”
— 1 Kings 12:28 (RSV)

63269.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
63269.question_text: Which of these kings did not assassinate his predecessor but was assassinated by his successor?
63269.explanation: Pekahiah was the son of Menahem and became king of Israel after his father's death. He reigned for two years in Samaria. During his reign, he did not kill his predecessor but continued the policies of his father. However, Pekahiah was assassinated by his own commander-in-chief, Pekah son of Remaliah, who then became the king of Israel. This sequence of events indicates that Pekahiah did not assassinate his predecessor but was himself assassinated by his successor.
